clue.text: One could raise a stink about charging post office rent

indicators.note: charging in the sense of rushing into, so the letters for about storm into the middle of the rent word

parts.note: to rent out is to let
CA, short for circa, means about

explanation.surface: A complaint about the Post Office demanding rent, the kind of thing that could cause a stink.
explanation.definitionFit: The polecat is a weasel-like animal notorious for the foul smell it gives off when threatened.

clue.text: Display part of book connected with soldier

parts.note: a page is part of a book
a soldier ant is a kind of ant, so ant can stand for soldier

explanation.surface: A display featuring a page from a book about a soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: A pageant is a lavish public show or procession, a spectacular display.

clue.text: Person going on the radio for prize

indicators.note: on the radio means as heard spoken, so a word with the same pronunciation is wanted

parts.note: a person going away is a leaver

explanation.surface: A departing presenter wins an award on air.
explanation.walkthrough: In British speech both words are pronounced LEE-ver. 'prize' is the verb, as in prize open.
explanation.definitionFit: To prize a lid off is to lever it off, forcing it open with a bar.

clue.text: Dead bodies initially stashed in luggage under coach

indicators.note: in a down clue, under puts the luggage word below the coach word

parts.note: a railway coach is a car or carriage

indicators.note: in puts the first letter inside the luggage word

parts.note: cases are luggage

indicators.note: initially signals the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A crime story: corpses tucked into the bags stowed beneath a coach.
explanation.definitionFit: Carcasses are the dead bodies of animals, or more loosely of people.

clue.text: Criminal act destroying spa in part of Barnet

indicators.note: destroying the spa means removing those letters from the criminal act word

parts.note: trespass is an offence, a criminal act

explanation.surface: Someone vandalises a health spa in Barnet, a district of north London.
explanation.walkthrough: Barnet, also a London borough, is rhyming slang: Barnet Fair means hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A tress is a long lock of hair, so it is part of one's barnet.

clue.text: Father trapped after losing head is feeling anxious

parts.note: FR is the abbreviation for Father, a priest's title

indicators.note: losing its head means the first letter of the word for trapped is dropped

parts.note: trapped means caught

explanation.surface: A priest, cornered and decapitated, is understandably on edge.
explanation.definitionFit: Fraught describes a person or situation full of tension and worry, so it serves as an adjective for anxious.

clue.text: He holds the line, angling for a job

definitions.text: He holds the line, angling for a job

parts.words: He holds the line, angling for a job
parts.note: sounds like a job-seeker waiting on the phone, but describes someone with a rod and line whose work is angling

explanation.surface: A caller waiting on hold, hoping to land employment.
explanation.definitionFit: A professional angler holds a fishing line, catching fish being their trade.

clue.text: Reporter's sanctioned within scope of hearing

indicators.note: a reporter speaks, so what follows is a word heard, matched by one spelt differently

parts.note: sanctioned means allowed

explanation.surface: A journalist is permitted to stay where things can be overheard.
explanation.definitionFit: Spoken out loud means audibly, said so others can hear it.

clue.text: Argue about receiving advance payment as collateral

indicators.note: receiving means taking in, so the stake is placed inside the shuffled letters
about means moved around, so the letters of argue are rearranged

parts.note: an ante is a stake paid in advance in poker

explanation.surface: Haggling over a deposit offered as security for a loan.
explanation.definitionFit: A guarantee is a pledge given as security, which is what collateral is.

clue.text: Singer, speaker and social media influencer?

definitions.meaning: a bird that tweets is a singer
a small loudspeaker for high notes
someone who posts tweets online; the question mark flags the playful sense

explanation.surface: A list of a celebrity's roles: vocalist, orator and online personality.
explanation.definitionFit: Tweeter covers a chirping bird, a treble loudspeaker unit and a person posting on Twitter.

clue.text: Teacher's conjecture obtaining accomplished name for university

indicators.note: the conjecture word obtains, or takes in, the replacement letters
for signals that the new letters stand in place of the university letter

parts.note: a conjecture is a guess
something accomplished is over, finished

explanation.surface: A tutor guesses that a degree-holder gained a distinguished name in place of a university.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is 'Teacher's', read as 'teacher is', with the rest of the clue as wordplay; 'for university' says what is replaced.
explanation.definitionFit: A governess is a woman employed to educate children privately in their home, a type of private tutor.

clue.text: Clear one's throat but not expect to speak

indicators.note: but not instructs us to keep the long word apart from the following word inside it

parts.note: to expectorate is to cough up phlegm, clearing one's throat
taken as written

explanation.surface: Advice to a nervous orator: cough first, but do not presume you will get to talk.
explanation.definitionFit: To orate is to deliver a formal speech, often in a pompous manner.

clue.text: What helps maintain circulation in a naked man?

indicators.note: naked means stripped of its covering, so the outer letters of the man word are removed

parts.note: a man is a mortal, a human being

explanation.surface: A riddle asking what keeps blood moving in an unclothed human.
explanation.definitionFit: The aorta is the body's main artery, carrying blood from the heart around the circulatory system.

clue.text: Constant change affecting most fads and tastes

indicators.note: a change affecting the letters reorders them into a new word
most of a word means all but its last letter

explanation.surface: Fashion commentary: unending change touches nearly every fad and taste.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most' trims FADS to FAD; FAD plus TASTES is then rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Steadfast means firm and unwavering, the same as constant in loyalty or purpose.

clue.text: Change answer drained teacher's put before class

indicators.note: put before places the earlier letters in front of the class word
drained means emptied of its contents, leaving only the outside letters of the teacher word

parts.note: a form is a class in a British school

explanation.surface: A tired teacher sets an answer in front of a class to alter things.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer abbreviation comes first in the clue, but 'put before class' only fixes where the class word goes; 'drained' keeps just the outer letters of 'teacher'.
explanation.definitionFit: To transform is to alter something completely in form or character, a stronger synonym for change.

clue.text: When one stops being bearer of misinformation

parts.note: as can mean when, as in as I left

indicators.note: stops means plugs a gap, so the one letter fills a space in the being word

parts.note: a being is a person
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A paradox about the moment someone stops spreading falsehoods.
explanation.definitionFit: An aspersion is a damaging, usually unfounded remark, so it carries false claims about someone.

clue.text: Some metallic sounds when reflected vary in frequency

indicators.note: reflected as in a mirror, so the letters are read backwards
some of the following words means a run of their letters is taken

explanation.surface: Metallic noises bouncing back fluctuate in pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: Read backwards, 'metallic so' gives OS CILLATEM, and 'Some' takes the run inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To oscillate is to swing back and forth, and in physics varying frequency is a regular oscillation.

clue.text: Miserable time to spend week in Bury

indicators.note: to spend the week is to use it up, so the week letter disappears from the season

parts.note: winter is the bleak, miserable season

explanation.surface: A grim period to pass a week in Bury, the Lancashire town.
explanation.walkthrough: Bury looks like the place name, the Lancashire town, but it is the verb. WINTER loses W.
explanation.definitionFit: To inter is to place a body in a grave, which is to bury it.

clue.text: Mock student with no qualification? Quite the opposite!

indicators.note: with no tells us something is taken away
Quite the opposite! swaps the roles, so it is the qualification that loses the student, not the reverse

parts.note: a qualification is a limitation or restriction
L, for learner, stands for student

explanation.surface: Mocking a student who has no qualifications.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as 'qualification with no student', LIMITATION loses L. Qualification means restriction, not a diploma.
explanation.definitionFit: Mock as an adjective means fake or simulated, which is what an imitation is.

clue.text: Smart set will know these guys?

definitions.meaning: clever, experienced people are said to know the ...
guys are ... used to secure a tent or mast

explanation.surface: Fashionable people are bound to know these chaps.
explanation.definitionFit: Guy ropes hold tents and masts steady, and knowing the ropes is the idiom for being experienced.

clue.text: Short quote included in factual account

indicators.note: included in means put inside, so the shortened quote goes inside the factual word

parts.note: factual means real

indicators.note: short means cut off at the end, so the quote word loses its last letter

parts.note: to cite is to quote

explanation.surface: A brief quotation is found within a true report.
explanation.definitionFit: A recital is a detailed narration or listing of facts, an account of events.

clue.text: Revolutionary new pesticide really is beginning to wipe this creepy-crawly out

indicators.note: revolutionary means turned around, so the letters are rearranged
out tells us the following letters are taken out of the shuffled pool
beginning to points at the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: An advert boasting that a revolutionary pesticide finally wipes out a creepy-crawly.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearranged, NEW PESTICIDE holds this answer plus IS and W, the first letter of 'wipe'; 'out' removes those. 'really' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: A centipede is a many-legged arthropod, the kind of crawling bug people call a creepy-crawly.

clue.text: 7 get established

parts.note: to earn is to get money
EST is the abbreviation for established, as on shop signs

explanation.surface: A cross-reference: secure a deposit and become settled.
explanation.definitionFit: Earnest is money paid as a pledge or guarantee, as in earnest money on a deal.

clue.text: Shortened train addressed complaint of guards

indicators.note: guards means encloses, so the cured word wraps around the train word

parts.note: an illness or complaint that has been addressed has been cured
the train of a dress is its tail

explanation.surface: A long train was cut down after someone grumbled about the guards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'train' suggests a railway, but it is a dress's trailing tail.
explanation.definitionFit: To curtail is to cut short, so something curtailed has been shortened.

clue.text: Place to host final of competition?

definitions.text: Place to host final of competition?

indicators.note: to host means to accommodate, so the place word contains the extra letter

parts.note: an area is a place

indicators.note: final of points to the last letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Where should the big match be held?
explanation.definitionFit: An arena is a stadium built for staging contests, such as a cup final.

clue.text: Put off man avoiding cleansing product

indicators.note: avoiding means steering clear of, so the man word is removed

parts.note: detergent is a cleansing product
a gent is a man

explanation.surface: A man is repelled and steers clear of soap.
explanation.definitionFit: To deter is to discourage someone from acting, which is to put them off.

clue.text: Noun encapsulated by 'rage' possibly?

indicators.note: encapsulated by means held inside, so the noun letter is enclosed
possibly hints that the letters of rage may be arranged differently

parts.note: N is the grammatical abbreviation for noun

explanation.surface: A grammar puzzle: what noun does 'rage' capture?
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges RAGE to AGER, and N goes inside it. The whole clue is also the definition, since rage is an example of this noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Rage is extreme fury, so it is an instance of the noun meaning wrath.

clue.text: Cheap fare starts to get rail users back on the line

indicators.note: starts to signals the first letter of each following word
back on the means the end letter of that word

explanation.surface: Train companies offering budget fares to tempt passengers back onto the railway.
explanation.definitionFit: Gruel is a thin, cheap porridge, the classic poor man's food.

clue.text: Second husband's deserted three times

indicators.note: a husband who has deserted has left, so his letter leaves the word

parts.note: thrice means three times
H is the abbreviation for husband; the 's stands for has

explanation.surface: A man has walked out on his wife for a second time, or even a third.
explanation.definitionFit: A trice is a moment, as in 'in a trice', just as a second means a very short time.

clue.text: Characteristic praise follows statue's full unveiling

indicators.note: follows places the praise word after the stripped statue word
a full unveiling strips every outer layer, peeling the statue word down to its core letters

parts.note: taken as the word statue, the 's linking it to its unveiling
a tribute is an act of praise

explanation.surface: A speech of praise comes after a statue is properly unveiled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'full unveiling' strips STATUE layer by layer, TATU then AT.
explanation.definitionFit: An attribute is a quality or feature regarded as typical of someone, which is what a characteristic is.

clue.text: Mature policy takes precedence over those that came earlier

indicators.note: takes precedence over means comes in front, putting the policy word first

parts.note: a line is a policy, as in the party line
to mature is to age

explanation.surface: An insurance policy that has matured outranks those taken out before.
explanation.definitionFit: Lineage is ancestry, the forebears who came before someone in a family line.

clue.text: Lock service that's replayed after call

indicators.note: after places the service word behind the call word

parts.note: to ring someone is to call them on the phone
in tennis a let is a serve touching the net, which is played again

explanation.surface: A tennis scene: a serve is retaken after a line call.
explanation.walkthrough: Lock is a lock of hair, not a fastening.
explanation.definitionFit: A ringlet is a curled lock of hair.
